title: Replicating Planning-Ahead Behavior in Constrained Text Generation: Acrostic Poems in Open-Source Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Models that plan ahead over long horizons may be more capable of deceptive strategies. Detecting and characterizing planning mechanisms is directly relevant to monitoring for goal-directed deception. The link from acrostic planning to safety monitoring is clearly articulated.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TransformerLens and logit lens on Llama-3-8B-Instruct are well-supported. However, Llama-3-8B requires meaningful GPU memory, and the activation patching experiments require understanding of intermediate representations. Feasible with mentor support but not trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two comparisons (acrostic vs rhyme planning depth) plus patching experiments. The core logit lens analysis is focused, but adding the patching component and the comparison dimension broadens scope. Could be narrowed to just the logit lens comparison.
